title: Working tracker with real, saved data
goal: The Today screen from sketch v1, backed by IndexedDB, with tested date, streak and calendar logic and seven-day check-in
goalPlain: After this phase you can tick the starter habits for today and for any of the last seven days, see correct streaks and the six-month heatmap, and everything survives a reload.

tasks.title: Project skeleton: Vite + Preact + TypeScript + Vitest
tasks.spec:
Create the real app in `web/` (the repository root currently holds only `.orys/` and `.gitignore`). Base it on the sketch files in `.orys/sketch/code/web/` — copy `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json` and `package.json` as a starting point and adjust as below. Do not copy `src/seed.ts` or `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. `web/package.json`: name `habits-web`, private, type module. Dependencies: `preact` ^11.2, `idb` ^8.0. Dev dependencies: `@preact/preset-vite` ^2.10, `typescript` ^7.0, `vite` ^8.3, `vitest` (check the current version with `npm view vitest version` and pin the current major), `fake-indexeddb` (current version). Scripts: `dev`: `vite`; `build`: `tsc --noEmit && vite build`; `typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`; `test`: `vitest run`; `preview`: `vite preview`. `web/tsconfig.json`: as in the sketch (target ES2022, module/moduleResolution ESNext/bundler, jsx react-jsx with jsxImportSource preact, strict, noEmit, lib ES2022+DOM, types `vite/client`), including `src`. Prefer explicit `import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'` in tests over vitest globals. `web/vite.config.ts`: the preact plugin plus a vitest `test` section. The logic tests in this project do not need a DOM, so keep the default node environment; add jsdom only if a later task needs it. Copy `.orys/sketch/code/web/src/styles.css` to `web/src/styles.css` unchanged — it is the agreed design and later tasks build on its classes and CSS variables. Add `web/src/main.tsx` that renders a minimal placeholder (`

Habits

`) importing `./styles.css`, so the build has an entry point; a later task replaces it. Add `web/src/lib/smoke.test.ts` with one trivial passing test so the test gate runs from the start. Make sure `web/node_modules` and `web/dist` are ignored by the existing root `.gitignore`; extend it if not.
acceptance: `cd web && npm install` succeeds and creates a lockfile
`cd web && npm run typecheck` exits 0
`cd web && npm test` runs at least one test and exits 0
`cd web && npm run build` produces `web/dist/index.html` and exits 0
`web/src/styles.css` is byte-identical to `.orys/sketch/code/web/src/styles.css`
No file from `.orys/` is imported by anything in `web/src`

tasks.title: Date, streak and calendar logic with unit tests
tasks.spec:
Create `web/src/lib/dates.ts` and `web/src/lib/streaks.ts`, plus their tests. Start from `.orys/sketch/code/web/src/core.ts`, which has a working version of this logic, and harden it.

`dates.ts` — the only place that touches `Date`:
- `export type DayKey = string` — a local calendar day as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `keyOf(d: Date): DayKey` — local getFullYear/getMonth/getDate, zero-padded. Never `toISOString` (that shifts the day for anyone east or west of UTC).
- `dateOf(key: DayKey): Date` — local midnight (`new Date(y, m-1, d)`), never `new Date(string)`.
- `addDays(key: DayKey, n: number): DayKey` — calendar arithmetic through `Date.setDate`, so it crosses month ends, year ends, leap days and DST changes correctly.
- `diffDays(a: DayKey, b: DayKey): number` — whole calendar days from a to b.
- `todayKey(now: Date = new Date()): DayKey`.
- `lastNDays(today: DayKey, n: number): DayKey[]` — oldest first, ending at `today` inclusive.
- `heatmapWeeks(today: DayKey, months = 6): DayKey[][]` — columns of seven day keys, each column Monday..Sunday, starting at the Monday on or before (today minus `months` months) and running to the week containing `today`.
- `MONTH_SHORT` and `WEEKDAY_SHORT` constants as in the sketch.

`streaks.ts`:
- `export function streaks(done: ReadonlySet<DayKey>, today: DayKey): { current: number; longest: number }`.
- Current streak: count back from `today` while the day is in `done`; if `today` is not ticked, start from yesterday instead, so an unticked today does not break a running streak (unticked today AND unticked yesterday means 0).
- Longest streak: the longest run of consecutive calendar days anywhere in `done`.
- Pure, no `Date.now()` — `today` is always passed in.

Tests `web/src/lib/dates.test.ts` and `web/src/lib/streaks.test.ts` must cover at least: `addDays` across 2024-02-28 → 02-29 → 03-01 (leap year) and 2023-02-28 → 03-01 (non-leap); across 2024-12-31 → 2025-01-01; across spring-forward and autumn DST dates (e.g. 2025-03-30 and 2025-10-26) — at minimum assert that a 400-day walk with `addDays(k, 1)` never repeats a key and always advances exactly one calendar day; `keyOf` for a Date near local midnight; `diffDays` symmetry and sign; `lastNDays` length and ordering; `heatmapWeeks` returns columns of exactly 7, starts on a Monday, and the last column contains `today`. Streak tests: empty set → 0/0; single day → 1/1; unticked today with ticked yesterday → current counts yesterday backwards; unticked today and yesterday → current 0; a streak crossing a month boundary and 29 February 2024; longest when the longest run is in the past, not the current one.
acceptance: `streaks(new Set(), '2025-03-01')` returns `{ current: 0, longest: 0 }`
With every day from 2024-02-25 to 2024-03-02 ticked and today = 2024-03-02, `current` is 7
With yesterday ticked but today not, `current` counts the run ending yesterday; with neither ticked, `current` is 0
`heatmapWeeks` columns all have length 7, every column starts on a Monday, and the final column contains today
No function in `dates.ts` or `streaks.ts` calls `toISOString`, `Date.UTC` or `Date.now()` except `todayKey`'s default argument
`cd web && npm test -- src/lib/dates.test.ts src/lib/streaks.test.ts` passes
verifyCommands: cd web && npm test -- src/lib/dates.test.ts src/lib/streaks.test.ts

tasks.title: IndexedDB store for habits and ticks
tasks.spec:
Create `web/src/lib/types.ts`, `web/src/lib/db.ts` (IndexedDB access via the `idb` package) and `web/src/lib/db.test.ts`.

Types in `web/src/lib/types.ts`:
```ts
export type Habit = { id: string; name: string; color: string; order: number; archivedAt: number | null; createdAt: number };
export type Tick = { id: string; habitId: string; day: DayKey }; // id = `${habitId}|${day}`
```

Database `habits` version 1, object stores:
- `habits`, keyPath `id`.
- `ticks`, keyPath `id`, with index `by-habit` on `habitId` and index `by-day` on `day`.

Exported functions (all async, all returning plain data):
- `openDb()` — memoised `openDB` call with the upgrade that creates both stores and both indexes.
- `listHabits(): Promise<Habit[]>` — sorted by `order` ascending, then `createdAt`; includes archived ones.
- `putHabit(h: Habit): Promise<void>`; `deleteHabit(id)` — also removes that habit's ticks via the `by-habit` index, in one transaction.
- `createHabit(name: string, color: string): Promise<Habit>` — id from `crypto.randomUUID()`, `order` = max existing order + 1, `archivedAt: null`, `createdAt: Date.now()`.
- `reorderHabits(idsInOrder: string[]): Promise<void>` — rewrites `order` to the array index, in one transaction.
- `listTicks(habitIds?: string[]): Promise<Tick[]>` — all ticks, or those of the given habits.
- `setTick(habitId: string, day: DayKey, done: boolean): Promise<void>` — one `put` or one `delete` on the composite id; idempotent (setting an existing tick, or clearing a missing one, is not an error).
- `replaceAll(habits: Habit[], ticks: Tick[]): Promise<void>` — clears both stores and writes the given data in a single readwrite transaction (used later by import).

Keep all `idb` usage inside this file; nothing else in the app may import `idb`.

Tests use `fake-indexeddb`: `import 'fake-indexeddb/auto'` at the top, and delete/recreate the database between tests so they are independent. Cover: a created habit comes back from `listHabits`; `createHabit` gives increasing `order`; `reorderHabits` changes the returned order; `setTick(true)` twice then `listTicks` yields exactly one tick; `setTick(false)` removes it and is safe when nothing is there; `deleteHabit` removes the habit and its ticks but leaves another habit's ticks alone; `replaceAll` leaves exactly the given rows.
acceptance: Calling `setTick(id, '2025-01-01', true)` twice results in exactly one row in `listTicks()`
`setTick(id, '2025-01-01', false)` on a day with no tick resolves without throwing
`deleteHabit(a)` removes habit a and all of a's ticks while habit b's ticks remain
`reorderHabits([c, a, b])` makes `listHabits()` return c, a, b in that order
`replaceAll([], [])` leaves both stores empty
Only `web/src/lib/db.ts` imports `idb` (grep confirms)
`cd web && npm test -- src/lib/db.test.ts` passes

tasks.title: App state hook: load once, tick instantly, write through
tasks.spec:
Create `web/src/state.ts` exporting a Preact hook `useHabitStore()` built on `useState`/`useEffect` from `preact/hooks`.

State shape: `{ loading: boolean; habits: Habit[]; ticks: Record<string, Set<DayKey>> /* habitId -> days */; today: DayKey; selectedHabitId: string | null; catchUpDay: DayKey }`.

Behaviour:
- On mount, load habits and ticks from `web/src/lib/db.ts` in one go and build the `ticks` map. While loading, `loading` is true.
- First run (no habits in the database at all): create three starter habits so the screen is not empty — 'Morning run' #f97362, 'Read 20 pages' #5b9cf6, 'Meditate' #8b7bf0 — persisted via `createHabit`. Only when `listHabits()` returns an empty array, never on later loads. Do not port `.orys/sketch/code/web/src/seed.ts`; its fake 200-day history must not ship.
- `toggle(habitId, day)`: accepts any day key, used for today and for the last seven days. Update the in-memory state synchronously first (so the UI repaints on the same tap), then call `setTick` and await it; if the write rejects, roll the in-memory change back and keep the app usable. This is what makes ticking feel instant. Reject (no-op) days in the future and days older than `addDays(today, -6)` so the UI cannot write outside the editable window.
- `addHabit`, `renameHabit(id, name)`, `recolorHabit(id, color)`, `setArchived(id, boolean)`, `reorder(idsInOrder)` — each updates state and persists through `db.ts`.
- `selectHabit(id)` sets `selectedHabitId` and persists it in `localStorage` under `habits.selectedHabit`; on load, restore it, falling back to the first non-archived habit.
- `setCatchUpDay(day)` sets the day the catch-up block edits; it defaults to `addDays(today, -1)` and is clamped to the last seven days.
- Derived helpers: `activeHabits` (archivedAt === null, sorted by order), `editableDays` (`lastNDays(today, 7)`), and `streaksFor(habitId)` using `streaks()` from `web/src/lib/streaks.ts` with the store's `today`.
- `today` is computed once on mount with `todayKey()` and recomputed when the document becomes visible again (`visibilitychange`), so a tab left open overnight shows the new day; when `today` moves, re-clamp `catchUpDay`.

Add `web/src/state.test.ts` covering the pure parts that need no DOM: factor out and export `buildTickMap(ticks: Tick[])`, `toggleInMap(map, habitId, day)` and `isEditableDay(day, today)`, and test them — build round-trip, toggling on then off returns an equal map, toggling does not mutate the input, `isEditableDay` accepts today and today-6 and rejects tomorrow and today-7.
acceptance: `buildTickMap([{id:'h|2025-01-01',habitId:'h',day:'2025-01-01'}])` yields a map whose `h` set contains '2025-01-01'
`toggleInMap` returns a new object and leaves its input unchanged
Toggling the same day twice returns a map equal to the original
`isEditableDay` is true for today and for today minus 6 days, false for tomorrow and for today minus 7 days
`toggle` on a day outside the editable window changes neither state nor the database
The starter habits are created only when the database holds no habits
Nothing in `web/src` outside `lib/db.ts` imports `idb`, and nothing imports the sketch's `seed.ts`
`cd web && npm test -- src/state.test.ts` passes

tasks.title: Today screen as sketch v1, with seven-day check-in
tasks.spec:
Build the one screen the owner agreed on. Look at `.orys/sketch/v1/today-1280.png` and `.orys/sketch/v1/today-375.png` first — the result must match them, with the one addition described in point 5. Reuse `web/src/styles.css` as-is (copied in p1-setup) and port the components from `.orys/sketch/code/web/src/ui.tsx` into `web/src/components/` (`Tick`, `Check`, `Heat`, `Legend`, `prettyToday`), dropping the `Switcher` — the real app ships only the Today list, no tab switcher. `web/src/main.tsx` renders `` from `web/src/App.tsx`, which uses `useHabitStore()` from `web/src/state.ts` and renders, inside `.wrap`: 1. Header `.topbar`: `

Habits

`. No tab switcher, no new header controls. 2. `.sub` line: the long local date (e.g. 'Wednesday 18 November') followed by '· tap a circle to tick it off'. 3. `.progress`: the `.bar` filled to done/total of today's active habits and `N of M done`. 4. `.card.rows` list of active habits in `order`. Each row contains, left to right: the `.tick` circle (one tap toggles **today**, filled with the habit colour and showing the check when done), the `.row-name` (dimmed with class `done` when ticked), the 7-day `.spark`, and `.row-meta` with '🔥 current d' and 'best longest'. Tapping the name selects that habit for the heatmap (point 6). **The spark is interactive**: render each of its seven cells (`lastNDays(today, 7)`, oldest left, today rightmost) as a `
acceptance: The screen shows, top to bottom: title, date line, progress bar with 'N of M done', the habit rows card, the catch-up block (day chips plus a habit list), and the six-month heatmap card with its legend
Tapping a habit's circle toggles today and repaints the row, progress bar, streak numbers and heatmap immediately; the change is still there after a full page reload
Tapping any of the seven cells in a row's strip toggles that habit on that day; the streak numbers and the heatmap update at once and the change survives a reload
Selecting a different day chip switches the catch-up list to that day, and ticking a habit there writes that day — verified for a day three days ago as well as yesterday
All seven editable days are reachable at a 375 px viewport through the day chips, where the row strip is hidden
The catch-up block shows an 'all done' line instead of the list when every active habit is ticked for the selected day
Clicking a cell in the six-month heatmap changes nothing (it is not a button)
Tapping a habit's name changes which habit the bottom heatmap shows, and that choice survives a reload
There is no tab switcher anywhere in the UI and no `?d=` query parameter handling
At a 375 px viewport the page has no horizontal scrollbar (document.scrollWidth equals innerWidth)
Archived habits do not appear in the main list, the progress count or the catch-up list
`cd web && npm run build` exits 0

title: Managing habits, export/import and offline
goal: The bottom-bar buttons all work and the app opens without a network
goalPlain: After this phase you can create your own habits with a name and a colour, rename, recolour, reorder and archive them, download all your data as a JSON file and load it back, and open the app with no internet connection.

tasks.title: New habit, edit, archive and reorder
tasks.spec:
Add the habit management the sketch only drew as dead buttons. Reuse the existing `.card`, `.btn`, `.btn.primary`, `.row` and `.swatch` styles in `web/src/styles.css`; add new classes only where nothing fits, in the same visual language (dark panels, 14 px radius, muted labels).

1. `web/src/components/HabitDialog.tsx` — a modal built on the native `<dialog>` element, used for both 'New habit' and 'Edit habit'. Fields: a text input for the name (required, trimmed, 1–40 characters) and a colour picker as a row of eight preset swatches from the sketch palette (#f97362, #5b9cf6, #8b7bf0, #39b58a, #e4b03a plus three more in the same tone) with the selected one outlined. Buttons: Cancel, Save, and in edit mode also 'Archive' (or 'Unarchive' when the habit is archived). Saving an empty or whitespace-only name is blocked with an inline message, not an alert. Escape and the backdrop close the dialog without saving.
2. Bottom bar in `web/src/App.tsx`: the `.footbar` from the sketch with '+ New habit' (primary), 'Reorder', and — added by the next task — 'Export JSON' and 'Import'. '+ New habit' opens the dialog in create mode and calls `addHabit`; the new habit appears at the end of the list straight away.
3. Each habit row gets a small 'Edit' icon button at its right, opening the dialog in edit mode for that habit. It must not sit where it can be hit instead of the one-tap circle or the seven-day strip; match the small 'Edit' button style used in the sketch's card direction.
4. 'Reorder' toggles a reorder mode in which each row shows up/down buttons instead of the streak numbers; moving a row calls `reorder(idsInOrder)` from the store. A 'Done' button leaves the mode. No drag-and-drop library.
5. Archiving: the habit disappears from the main list, the progress count and the catch-up list, but its ticks are kept. Add a collapsed 'Archived (N)' section under the bottom bar listing archived habits with an 'Unarchive' button; hide the section when N is 0.

Unit-test the pure helpers in `web/src/lib/habits.test.ts`: a `moveInArray(ids, from, to)` helper used by reorder (moving the first item down, the last item up, and a no-op move at the edges) and a `validateHabitName(raw)` helper returning the trimmed name or an error reason (empty, whitespace-only, over 40 characters).
acceptance: '+ New habit' creates a habit with the entered name and chosen colour; it appears in the list and is still there after a reload
Editing a habit's name and colour updates the row, its seven-day strip and its heatmap colour
Saving a name that is empty or only whitespace is refused with a visible message and no habit is created or changed
Archiving removes the habit from the main list, the 'N of M done' count and the catch-up list, while its ticks remain in the database
An archived habit can be unarchived from the 'Archived (N)' section and returns to the list with its history intact
Reorder mode moves a habit up or down and the new order survives a reload
`moveInArray` at the first/last index is a no-op and never loses or duplicates an id
`cd web && npm test -- src/lib/habits.test.ts` passes

tasks.title: Export to JSON and import back
tasks.spec:
Make the 'Export JSON' and 'Import' buttons in the `.footbar` real.

`web/src/lib/backup.ts`:
- `export type Backup = { version: 1; exportedAt: string; habits: Habit[]; ticks: Tick[] }`.
- `toBackup(habits, ticks): Backup` — `exportedAt` is an ISO timestamp for display only; the day keys inside stay `YYYY-MM-DD` strings and must not be reformatted.
- `parseBackup(text: string): { ok: true; data: Backup; dropped: number } | { ok: false; error: string }` — validates that it is JSON, that `version` is 1, that `habits` is an array of objects with string `id`, `name`, `color`, numeric `order`, `archivedAt` null-or-number, and that `ticks` is an array with string `id`, `habitId` and a `day` matching `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/`. Ticks whose `habitId` is not among the habits are dropped and counted in `dropped`. Never throws — malformed input returns `{ ok: false, error }` with a message fit to show the user.

UI in `web/src/App.tsx`:
- 'Export JSON' builds the backup from the current store, serialises it with two-space indentation, and downloads it through a `Blob` + object URL as `habits-YYYY-MM-DD.json` (today's local date), revoking the URL afterwards.
- 'Import' opens a hidden `<input type="file" accept="application/json">`. After reading the file, show a confirmation dialog (reuse the `<dialog>` pattern from `HabitDialog`) stating plainly: 'This replaces all N habits and M ticks currently stored. Continue?'. On confirm, call `replaceAll` from `web/src/lib/db.ts` and reload the store state so the screen shows the imported data without a page refresh. On a parse failure, show the error in the dialog and change nothing.

Tests in `web/src/lib/backup.test.ts`: round trip `parseBackup(JSON.stringify(toBackup(h, t)))` returns the same habits and ticks; not-JSON input returns ok:false; a wrong `version` returns ok:false; a tick with an unknown habitId is dropped and counted; a tick with day '2025-1-1' or '01/01/2025' is rejected; an empty backup (no habits, no ticks) parses successfully.
acceptance: Clicking 'Export JSON' downloads a file named `habits-<today>.json` containing every habit and tick
Importing a file exported from this app restores exactly the same habits and ticks and the screen updates without a page refresh
Importing a non-JSON or wrong-version file shows an error message and leaves the existing data untouched
The import confirmation names how many habits and ticks will be replaced, and cancelling changes nothing
Ticks referring to a habit not in the file are dropped rather than imported as orphans
`cd web && npm test -- src/lib/backup.test.ts` passes

tasks.title: Offline: manifest and service worker
tasks.spec:
Make the built app open with no network, which the sketch explicitly left out. Add `vite-plugin-pwa` (check the current version with `npm view vite-plugin-pwa version`) as a dev dependency and configure it in `web/vite.config.ts` with `registerType: 'autoUpdate'`, precaching the built assets (`globPatterns: ['**/*.{js,css,html,svg,png,webmanifest}']`) and a web app manifest: name 'Habits', short name 'Habits', `display: 'standalone'`, `background_color` and `theme_color` `#0f1115` (the app background from `styles.css`), `start_url: '/'`. Add a simple icon at 192 and 512 px in `web/public/` — a plain coloured rounded square with a check mark in the accent colour #39b58a; do not pull in an icon library.

Add `<meta name="theme-color" content="#0f1115">` to `web/index.html`.

Register the service worker from `web/src/main.tsx` using the plugin's virtual module, guarded so it is a no-op in development and in tests. The app must keep working if registration fails (for example on a non-secure origin) — wrap it in a try/catch and never block rendering on it.

Do not add any runtime caching rule for external hosts: the app makes no network requests at all.

After building, serve `web/dist` with `npm run preview`, load it once, then confirm in the browser that reloading with the network disabled still shows the app with its data.
acceptance: `cd web && npm run build` emits a service worker and a `manifest.webmanifest` into `web/dist`
`web/dist/manifest.webmanifest` declares name 'Habits', standalone display and icons at 192 and 512 px
Loading the preview build once and then reloading it with the network offline still shows the habit list and the stored ticks
The dev server still starts and the app renders with no service worker registered in development
Service worker registration failing does not prevent the app from rendering
`cd web && npm test` still passes
